summary.text: Tony Simone is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent seeking re-election to a third term representing Manhattan's West Side, including Chelsea, Hell's Kitchen and Midtown. Before his 2022 election he worked in government and the nonprofit sector, including for state and city elected officials, People for the American Way and Friends of Hudson River Park. His official biography says he is focused on public safety, mental health, affordable housing, health care, climate change, tenant and immigrant rights, and equity for disabled people and LGBTQ+ New Yorkers.

paragraphs.text: Simone was born in Queens, New York, in 1970. His mother was born in Peru and immigrated to New York City in 1968; his father, born in Astoria, drove taxis and trucks, and his late grandfather was a Teamsters union delegate.

He received a BA in political science and a BS in applied economics from Hofstra University (1994, per Ballotpedia) and an MPA from Columbia University's School of International and Public Affairs (2001, per Ballotpedia).

He began his government career working for the late state Sen. Catherine Abate and for then-City Councilmember Christine Quinn, and also worked in the office of New York State Comptroller H. Carl McCall.
Simone later served as deputy director of the northeast regional office of People for the American Way, where he led policy and field operations and organized on immigrant and LGBT rights.

He returned to government as Director of Community Outreach for the NYC Council under Speaker Christine Quinn, where his official biography says he directed volunteer relief efforts after Superstorm Sandy, led local initiatives to reduce hate crimes, advocated for marriage equality and worked to protect tenants.
Immediately before the Assembly, he was Director of External Affairs at Hudson River Park Friends, working on fundraising and advocacy for the waterfront park.

Simone was elected to the Assembly in 2022, defeating Republican Joseph A. Maffia with 84.7% of the vote in the November 8 general election, and took office January 1, 2023; he was re-elected in 2024 with 99.1% of the vote.
His district covers Chelsea, Hell's Kitchen, Midtown and part of the Lincoln Center area.

His current Assembly committee memberships are Corporations, Authorities and Commissions; Economic Development, Job Creation, Commerce and Industry; Election Law; Environmental Conservation; Governmental Operations; and Labor, and he is also a member of the Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic & Asian Legislative Caucus, the Task Force on New Americans and the Puerto Rican/Hispanic Task Force.
His official biography says he has been a campaign volunteer and staffer for decades, and that he lives in Hell's Kitchen with his husband, Jason, and their rescue dog.
